capitals.name: Monte Albán
capitals.note: Infobox 17°2′38″N 96°46′4″W; 'Founded toward the end of the Middle Formative period at around 500 BC'; 'largely abandoned' c. 900–1000. The Zapotec page's infobox gives Monte Albán as capital '700 BC – AD 700', then Mitla de facto 700–1400.

keyframe_review.note: 6,447 km2 ≈ the Valley of Oaxaca (bbox -97.41..-96.26, 16.74..17.71): Monte Albán Early I and Late I 'c. 500–300 BCE and 300–100 BCE'; 'a population estimate of around 5,200 by the end of the following Monte Albán Ia phase (c. 300 BCE)'. No infobox area on either page.
Identical shape. The Zapotec page: the state 'began to expand during the late Monte Alban 1 phase (400–100 BC)', still inside the valley. Cliopatria's -291 split has no event behind it.

correction.text: Monte Albán II (c. 100 BCE – CE 200): 'Monte Albán expanded militarily, through cooption, and via outright colonization' to 'the Cañada de Cuicatlán to the north and the southern Ejutla and Sola de Vega valleys'; the Isthmus of Tehuantepec is on neither page and is removed

keyframe_review.note: 69,768 km2 (about three quarters of Oaxaca state) from -91: the timing matches Monte Albán II (c. 100 BCE); the extent is generous. The pages name the Cañada de Cuicatlán, Ejutla, Sola de Vega and 'much of the Oaxacan highlands'; neither names the Isthmus or the Pacific coast, so a 90 km radius around Tehuantepec is removed (about 47,300 km2 remain). No infobox area to compare.

correction.text: Monte Albán IIIA (c. CE 200–500): 'dominating influence over the Valley of Oaxaca and across much of the Oaxacan highlands'; Isthmus removed as for -91

keyframe_review.note: Same shape as -91; the IIIA text supports the highlands, not the Isthmus. 'Monte Albán had an estimated population of 17,200' in phase II; 'high-level contacts between the site's elites and those at the powerful central Mexican city of Teotihuacan' are undated.

correction.text: Late Classic begins (Monte Albán IIIB/IV, c. CE 500–1000); shape as for 207 with the Isthmus removed

keyframe_review.note: The city 'lost its political pre-eminence by the end of the Late Classic (c. AD 500–750)'; Cliopatria's shrink in 602 falls inside that window and is kept (ledger 602, confidence 1).

8,550 km2 ≈ the Valley of Oaxaca again, 602..891: the diminished Monte Albán of IIIB/IV. The page dates the loss of pre-eminence only to 'c. AD 500–750'; Cliopatria's 602 is kept. (Review am-01, 2026-10-18: Cliopatria's 602 shape lies east and south of Monte Albán (10 of its 31 grid cells fall within 40 km of Oaxaca, and the capital's cell is about 17 km outside it), so the 40 km Valley of Oaxaca radius the ledger keeps after the 602 loss is added; verdict ok changed to adjust)

correction.text: the Valley of Oaxaca around Monte Albán plus Cliopatria's eastern valleys, 602..891: the city 'lost its political pre-eminence by the end of the Late Classic (c. AD 500–750)' but was 'largely abandoned' only 'By the end of the same period (c. AD 900–1000)'
Cliopatria shape plus the 40 km Valley of Oaxaca radius around Monte Albán (as for 602); years 892..900: 'By the end of the same period (c. AD 900–1000), the ancient capital was largely abandoned'

keyframe_review.note: Years only: Cliopatria ends the row in 895; the dossier ends the state in 900 (the Zapotec page's phase table ends Monte Alban 3 at 'c. 200-900').

region.text: the Y-shaped Central Valleys of Oaxaca

ledger.note: 500 BC: Monte Albán is founded on an empty hilltop above the Valley of Oaxaca. 'Founded toward the end of the Middle Formative period at around 500 BC'; 'the Monte Alban hills appear to have been uninhabited prior to 500 BCE'. 'By 500 BCE, with the emergence of Monte Albán as the area's main city, San José Mogote's 1000 years of dominance ended' (San José Mogote page); 'Zapotec civilization originated in the Y-shaped Central Valleys of Oaxaca in the late 6th century BC' (Zapotec page). San José Mogote was a village chiefdom, not a state; no dossier.

region.text: 'the Cañada de Cuicatlán to the north and the southern Ejutla and Sola de Vega valleys' and 'much of the Oaxacan highlands'

ledger.note: 100 BC: Monte Albán expands beyond the valley. In Monte Albán II (c. 100 BCE – CE 200) 'Monte Albán expanded militarily, through cooption, and via outright colonization' into 'the Cañada de Cuicatlán to the north and the southern Ejutla and Sola de Vega valleys'; 'Zapotec conquest there has been confirmed through archaeological survey and excavations'; Building J holds 'more than 40 large, carved slabs dating to Monte Albán II' naming conquered places. The conquered valleys were chiefdoms without Cliopatria rows, hence 'nobody'. Cliopatria's shape grows in -91.

region.text: the outer valleys and highlands beyond the Valley of Oaxaca

ledger.note: c. 500–750: Monte Albán loses its political pre-eminence and the outer valleys fall away. 'The city lost its political pre-eminence by the end of the Late Classic (c. AD 500–750)'. The year 602 is Cliopatria's keyframe inside that window, not the page's; confidence 1.

region.text: the Valley of Oaxaca; 'the ancient capital was largely abandoned'

ledger.note: c. 900: Monte Albán is largely abandoned and the valley's centres go their own way. 'By the end of the same period (c. AD 900–1000), the ancient capital was largely abandoned'; other centres 'began to assert their autonomy, including sites such as Cuilapan and Zaachila in the Valle Grande' and 'Lambityeco, Mitla, and El Palmillo in the eastern Tlacolula arm'. The Zapotec page's phase table ends Monte Alban 3 at c. 900 and gives Mitla as de facto capital 700–1400. The Postclassic Zapotec city-states (Zaachila, Mitla) need a dossier from the post-900 Mesoamerica group; until then the land goes to nobody.

wars.name: Monte Albán II conquests (Building J slabs)
belligerents: Cañada de Cuicatlán and southern valley chiefdoms

zones.text: the Cañada de Cuicatlán, Ejutla and Sola de Vega valleys

wars.outcome: Monte Albán incorporated the Cañada de Cuicatlán and the Ejutla and Sola de Vega valleys 'militarily, through cooption, and via outright colonization'; 'Some of the places listed on Building J slabs have been tentatively identified'.
wars.note: A span, not a dated war: Monte Albán II is c. 100 BCE – CE 200 on the page. No contest zone is drawn because the page dates no campaign.

certainty.note: Archaeological-survey frontiers only; the Isthmus and the coast are kept outside the state on the researcher's reading.

notes: Cliopatria's 'Zapotec Civilization' row (-500..895; Seshat ids mx_monte_alban_1_early … mx_monte_alban_3_b_4) is the Monte Albán state, not the whole Zapotec culture (which the Zapotec page runs c. 700 BC – AD 1521). The dossier is therefore written as Monte Albán under the Cliopatria slug, and no separate 'monte-alban' slug was created, so that two dossiers do not claim the same seven shapes; if the orchestrator prefers the slug monte-alban, rename the file and keep cliopatria_names. The row is one continuous state (one capital, -500..c. 900), not successive states, so it is not split. Disagreements: the Zapotec page's infobox gives Monte Albán as capital 700 BC – AD 700 and its phase table ends Monte Alban 2 at AD 100 while its text says AD 200; the Monte Albán page's chronology (I 500–100 BCE, II 100 BCE–CE 200, IIIA 200–500, IIIB/IV 500–1000) is followed. The 602 shrink rests on Cliopatria (confidence 1). Gazetteer names lacking: Valley of Oaxaca, Cañada de Cuicatlán, Ejutla, Sola de Vega, Isthmus of Tehuantepec (a 40 km radius around Oaxaca city and a 90 km radius around Tehuantepec stand in). The Seshat page https://seshat-db.com/core/polity/mx_monte_alban_3_b_4 did not load. Teotihuacan contacts (the Oaxaca barrio at Teotihuacan; a Teotihuacan-style 'guest house' at Monte Albán) are undated on both pages. Postclassic successors (Zaachila, Mitla, the Mixtec intrusion, the Aztec conquest of 1458, Guiengola 1497–1502) are outside this group's scope and belong to the post-900 Mesoamerica group.
